source_text: ok, it occurs to me that maybe I should create a variant of report-emacs-bug, like report-futon-bug that would log context etc so I don't have to think about the bugs, I could just bell them out.  that could even ho to an agent on lucy or metameso, so the bug report would have to be relatively self contained

reply_text:
㊣ ("report-futon-bug") Good idea. It's the same shape as `report-emacs-bug`: the tool gathers its own state, so you only supply a one-line description. I've added it to the alternative backlog (§5, futon0 `65fcd5f`) as an idea with a design sketch.

🈖 (the sketch) `M-x report-futon-bug` asks for one line, typed or dictated, and gathers the rest:
- the region, or the tail of the current REPL buffer
- `*Messages*` and `*Backtrace*`
- recent journal lines for futon3c, futon1b and emacs-graph
- Agency and futon1b health, plus a zone-health summary
- the HEAD sha and dirty status of each futon repo
- host, time and Emacs version

It writes all of that to **one self-contained markdown file with secrets scrubbed**. Tokens do turn up in environments and logs, and the file is going to another machine. Then it bells the file with `--mode work` to a triage agent whose brief is: reproduce, locate, propose a fix, bell back. Without `--mode work` a bell runs nothing but still reports done, per your memory notes. There's already precedent in the stack: `session-turn-analysis.el` dispatches through `agency_send.py` from Emacs, so the plumbing exists.

㊩ ("go to an agent on lucy or metameso") One constraint you'd hit today: zone-health shows the federation peers **unreachable from zone**, and the roster here lists no lucy or metameso agents. A bell to them would fail. So in a first version, the self-contained file would itself be the transport. It's committed to git, any host can pull it, and the bell goes to a local seat. Once federation is fixed (README-hardening §6), the same report could go straight to a remote agent.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I build it? Under the coding-handoff protocol this would normally go to a Codex seat. It's one Elisp file plus a small collector script, and I'd review it. Or would you rather leave it in the backlog for now?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-13
previous_reply_acts.text:
(done) The warn hook is in and working:
- **Script:** `futon3c/scripts/claude-hooks/bg_warn.py` (futon3c `66da03c9`).
- **Wiring:** `~/.claude/settings.json`, PreToolUse on `Bash|Monitor`. The old file is kept as `settings.json.bak-2026-10-10`.
- **Who it warns:** only pouch agents, meaning `FUTON_AGENT_ID` is set, so terminal sessions are left alone.
- **What it catches:** `run_in_background`, `nohup`/`setsid`/`disown`, a trailing `&`, and any Monitor call.
- **How it warns:** the agent gets a note telling it to use `bg.py launch "<cmd>" --agent <id>`, with "if it finishes within this turn, ignore this" for short jobs. It never blocks a command.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-13
previous_reply_acts.text: (checked) The pipe test covered 8 cases. `2>&1`, `&&`, commands that already use bg.py, and sessions without an agent id all stay silent. I also proved it live in this session: my own `sleep 0.1 &` produced the warning in my context, and the command still ran. The backlog entry in §5 is now marked **adopted** (futon0 `e661585`).

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-13
previous_reply_acts.text: (scope) Other pouches pick it up the next time they load settings. Any pouch that's warm right now may need a fresh turn or a restart first. If the warning turns out to be too soft, the next step would be to deny `run_in_background` alone and keep warning on the rest.
